tip_title: Peak Hurricane Season Is Here. One Thing To Do Before a Storm Is Named.
blurb:
💡 **Insurance Tip: Peak Hurricane Season Is Here. One Thing To Do Before a Storm Is Named.**

August and September are statistically the most active weeks of Atlantic hurricane season. Here's the thing most people don't realize: once a named storm is in the forecast, insurers can issue binding restrictions that prevent you from making any changes to your policy until after the threat has passed. That means now — before any storm is named — is the window to call your agent and confirm your coverage is actually in order. The big things to check: does your policy have a separate wind or hurricane deductible (these are usually percentage-based, not a flat dollar amount), and do you have flood coverage in place? A standard homeowners policy covers wind damage, but it does not cover flooding. Those are two separate policies, and you want both lined up before you need them.

Not sure what your hurricane deductible actually is, or whether you have flood coverage? Your Peachy agent can pull up your declarations page and walk through both questions with you — usually takes about ten minutes.

📖 [Learn more from Ready.gov](https://www.ready.gov/hurricane-toolkit)
summary: Covers the August-September peak of hurricane season as a prompt to review binding restrictions, hurricane/wind deductibles, and flood coverage gaps before a named storm triggers insurer lockouts — distinct from prior tips on percentage-deductible mechanics and pre-season prep checklists.
